CONTACT → SUSPENSION → RIDER

Two tyres. One moving bike.

Launch a hardtail or full-suspension bike over a trail, a square edge or a coarse faceted rock. Distributed tyre contacts drive frame motion, suspension travel and a passive rider guide or moving articulated rider.

Bike & launch

SI UNITS
Drive and braking

Each row replaces all three controls at its time. Positive rear drive rolls forward. Brake values are torque capacities; solved torque may be lower. Times must align to the integration step.

Calculation runs offline before playback. Launch velocity is an initial condition. Grip couples wheel spin and travel through each deformed contact. This is a homogeneous interface coefficient, not a calibrated material preset.

Velocities are relative to each rotating hub. Node 0 starts at the bottom of the reference ring and rotates with it. Nonuniform RMS removes mean node translation. Contact power is signed soft-contact work; it is not all dissipation. Maxima are across nodes at the displayed sample; motion between observations can be missed. No force or damping law is changed.

Forces and motion over time

Supported experiment

Both deformable wheels belong to the same translating and pitching bike. Fork, rear linkage and passive rider forces respond to those contacts. Hardtail rear attachment stays rigid. Progressive buffers act before ultimate travel limits.

Uncalibrated and planar, with optional homogeneous Coulomb friction. Soft constraints may creep under sustained load. Authored sharp edges and low-resolution facets are retained. Corner forces remain sensitive to tyre resolution. Hub drive and dry-friction brakes act between wheel and carrier. No frame collision, inflation law, chain/crank model, brake heating, steering, anatomical calibration, saddle support, layered soil or damage. Contact overlap, rim clearance, deformation, pitch and component travel limits stop unsupported motion. No real-time performance claim. Brake holding is regularized, with possible creep; it is not an exact wheel lock. Articulated mode uses independent chassis properties and bounded passive joint domains; it stops before unsupported joint motion. There is no active pumping or manoeuvre controller yet.

Rider poses · standing and sitting study

Compare starting geometry with hands and feet fixed. These illustrative 70 kg poses are independent of the bike run above. Changing this study does not move the simulated rider.

A low hip position expresses seating intent only. There is no saddle contact here, and no supported sit/stand transition. Body lengths, masses and attachment locations remain the same in every example. Paired limbs are aggregated; no anatomical or collision validation is implied.

Frame-local coordinates: x forward, z up. Trunk pitch is measured from vertical (+z), positive toward forward (+x).

Orange: selected pose. Dashed grey: reference unseated pose. Hollow circles: whole-rider centres of mass. Cyan: fixed hand and foot attachments. Trunk ends at the shoulder; no separate head or pelvis body is drawn.

Rider task targets · shift and crouch preview

Inspect sampled joint goals from a hip and trunk request. Hands and feet stay at the reference study anchors. This independent geometry study is available with either bike; it does not read or change the applied bike run.

Start: hip −0.15 / 0.25 m, trunk 0.55 rad. Commands are 0.01 s apart; x points forward and z up. Hip and trunk requests interpolate linearly. Every sampled target must satisfy reach, bend and the original passive joint domains. No target is clamped.

Orange: target geometry. Grey: unchanged starting geometry. Hollow circles: whole-rider COM, distinct from the hip. Cyan: retained attachments. These are targets, not measured motion.

Unbound rider · short free-flight probe

Inspect the passive rider on its own for 0.02 seconds. This uses an authored world pose and velocity; it does not release the rider from the bike run above.

No bike, ground or collision is present. This planar experiment checks body motion and accounting; it is not a crash, jump or anatomical calibration. Initial and final poses may overlap because the motion is brief.

Dashed grey: initial pose. Orange: last accepted pose. Cyan points: recorded whole-rider centre of mass. Equal x/z scale, without motion magnification.

Last accepted time
COM · world x / z
Energy + loss residual · signed
Passive joint damping loss
Momentum residual · world x / z
Angular momentum residual · about rider COM

The energy residual compares native energy plus accumulated damping loss with its initial value. Linear momentum subtracts gravity impulse; angular momentum is about the moving rider COM. Small residuals include timestep error, not unexplained physical damping. Guards are checked each step; a stopped run retains the last accepted state. Passing guards does not establish accuracy for arbitrary body or joint parameters.
